biography: Gerson Campos, a name synonymous with unwavering consistency in the modern racing world, hails from the vibrant streets of São Paulo, Brazil. His journey began not on the asphalt, but on the dirt tracks of his grandfather's fazenda, where he honed his car control skills drifting an old Volkswagen Beetle. Racing wasn't initially the goal; a scholarship to study engineering was. However, the roar of engines proved too alluring. He traded textbooks for tires, risking everything on a karting career funded by selling his prized guitar. His breakthrough came at the Brazilian National Karting Championship, where, despite starting last after a mechanical failure, he carved his way through the field to victory. Now, at 33, Campos is at his peak, a respected figure on the grid, known for his methodical approach and steely resolve, driving for his own self-titled team.
drivingStyle: Campos is a master of tire management and calculated aggression. He doesn't possess the flamboyant, all-or-nothing style of some of his contemporaries. Instead, he excels at preserving his equipment, maximizing his pace over the course of a race, and capitalizing on the mistakes of others. He prefers a smooth, controlled entry into corners, prioritizing a strong exit to maintain momentum. He rarely makes rash moves, but when he sees an opportunity, he pounces with clinical precision. His calm demeanor allows him to handle pressure situations with remarkable poise.

rivalries.name: Alessandro Rossi
rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from their karting days, fueled by contrasting personalities and aggressive on-track battles. Rossi is the flamboyant showman to Campos's quiet professional.

rivalries.name: Isabelle Dubois
rivalries.reason: A more recent rivalry ignited by a controversial incident at the Monaco Grand Prix, where Dubois accused Campos of blocking her during qualifying, costing her a potential pole position.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: Their rivalry is based on respect, but also the fight for best independent team in the championship. Both drivers have had very close results over the past few seasons.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky socks, gifted to him by his grandmother, for every race.
Listens to a specific Brazilian samba song before getting into the car, regardless of the track.
Spends five minutes in complete silence, meditating, before each qualifying session.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about going the fastest for one lap; it's about going consistently fast for every lap."
careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian Grand Prix in 2028, a dominant performance in front of his home crowd, fulfilling a lifelong dream.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out on the first lap of the 2026 Monaco Grand Prix after being caught in a multi-car pileup, resulting in a broken wrist and sidelining him for three races.
